sanskrit: hanumān api vikrāntaḥ sarvaṃ śuśrāva tattvataḥ sītāyās trijaṭāyāś ca rākṣasīnāṃ ca tarjanam
english: The valiant Hanūmān heard everything truly — the menacing of Sītā by Trijaṭā and by the demonesses.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇas tāṃ devīṃ devatām iva nandane tato bahuvidhāṃ cintāṃ cintayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Gazing upon that goddess-like lady as if she were a deity in a pleasure-grove, the monkey then turned over in his mind a great variety of thoughts.

sanskrit: yāṃ kapīnāṃ sahasrāṇi subahūny ayutāni ca dikṣu sarvāsu mārgante seyam āsāditā mayā
english: She whom many thousands and tens of thousands of monkeys are searching for in all directions — that very one has been reached by me.

sanskrit: cāreṇa tu suyuktena śatroḥ śaktim avekṣitā gūḍhena caratā tāvad avekṣitam idaṃ mayā
english: By moving in well-devised espionage, I have observed the strength of the enemy; moving covertly, all this has been surveyed by me.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ viśeṣaś ca purī ceyam avekṣitā rākṣasādhipater asya prabhāvo rāvaṇasya ca
english: The particulars of the rākṣasas and this city have been observed, as has the power of this lord of the rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ tasyāprameyasya sarvasattvadayāvataḥ samāśvāsayituṃ bhāryāṃ patidarśanakāṅkṣiṇīm
english: It is fitting that I console the wife of that immeasurable one, who is compassionate to all beings — she who longs to behold her husband.

sanskrit: aham āśvāsayāmy enāṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām adṛṣṭaduḥkhāṃ duḥkhasya na hy antam adhigacchatīm
english: I shall console her whose face resembles the full moon, who has never before known such suffering, and who now finds no end to her grief.

sanskrit: yadi hy aham imāṃ devīṃ śokopahatacetanām anāśvāsya gamiṣyāmi doṣavad gamanaṃ bhavet
english: For if I depart without consoling this lady whose mind is overwhelmed with grief, my departure would be blameworthy.

sanskrit: gate hi mayi tatreyaṃ rājaputrī yaśasvinī paritrāṇam avindantī jānakī jīvitaṃ tyajet
english: For when I have gone back, this glorious princess, Jānakī, finding no refuge, would abandon her life.

sanskrit: mayā ca sa mahābāhuḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanaḥ samāśvāsayituṃ nyāyyaḥ sītādarśanalālasaḥ
english: And that great-armed one whose face resembles the full moon, who yearns to behold Sītā — it is right that I console her on his behalf.

sanskrit: niśācarīṇāṃ pratyakṣam akṣamaṃ cābhibhāṣaṇam kathaṃ nu khalu kartavyam idaṃ kṛcchra gato hy aham
english: Speaking in the presence of these night-wandering demonesses is also not easy — how indeed is this to be accomplished? For I am in a difficult situation.

sanskrit: anena rātriśeṣeṇa yadi nāśvāsyate mayā sarvathā nāsti saṃdehaḥ parityakṣyati jīvitam
english: If I do not console her before the remainder of this night passes, there is no doubt whatsoever that she will abandon her life.

sanskrit: rāmaś ca yadi pṛcchen māṃ kiṃ māṃ sītābravīd vacaḥ kim ahaṃ taṃ pratibrūyām asaṃbhāṣya sumadhyamām
english: And if Rāma were to ask me, 'What word did Sītā speak to you?' — what could I reply to him, having spoken not at all to the slender-waisted one?

sanskrit: sītāsaṃdeśarahitaṃ mām itas tvarayā gatam nirdahed api kākutsthaḥ kruddhas tīvreṇa cakṣuṣā
english: Kākutstha, angry, might even burn me with his fierce gaze, seeing me returned from here in haste, bereft of any message from Sītā.

sanskrit: yadi ced yojayiṣyāmi bhartāraṃ rāmakāraṇāt vyartham āgamanaṃ tasya sasainyasya bhaviṣyati
english: And if I set her husband Rāma in motion because of this, the coming of him along with his army would be fruitless.

sanskrit: antaraṃ tv aham āsādya rākṣasīnām iha sthitaḥ śanair āśvāsayiṣyāmi saṃtāpabahulām imām
english: But finding an opportune moment, stationed here among the demonesses, I shall gently console her who is filled with anguish.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hy atitanuś caiva vanaraś ca viśeṣataḥ vācaṃ codāhariṣyāmi mānuṣīm iha saṃskṛtām
english: Though I am exceedingly small and especially a monkey, I shall speak here in the human tongue, in refined Sanskrit.

sanskrit: yadi vācaṃ pradāsyāmi dvijātir iva saṃskṛtām rāvaṇaṃ manyamānā māṃ sītā bhītā bhaviṣyati
english: If I were to speak in refined Sanskrit as a brahmin would, Sītā, thinking me to be Rāvaṇa, would become frightened.

sanskrit: avaśyam eva vaktavyaṃ mānuṣaṃ vākyam arthavat mayā sāntvayituṃ śakyā nānyatheyam aninditā
english: I must certainly speak a meaningful human word; there is no other way this blameless lady can be soothed.

sanskrit: seyam ālokya me rūpaṃ jānakī bhāṣitaṃ tathā rakṣobhis trāsitā pūrvaṃ bhūyas trāsaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Jānakī, seeing my form and hearing such speech, already frightened by the rākṣasas, will become frightened once more.

sanskrit: tato jātaparitrāsā śabdaṃ kuryān manasvinī jānamānā viśālākṣī rāvaṇaṃ kāmarūpiṇam
english: Then the high-minded, large-eyed lady, overcome with terror, knowing Rāvaṇa's ability to assume any form he wishes, would cry out.

sanskrit: sītayā ca kṛte śabde sahasā rākṣasīgaṇaḥ nānāpraharaṇo ghoraḥ sameyād antakopamaḥ
english: And at the cry raised by Sītā, the host of demonesses, terrible and armed with various weapons, resembling Death itself, would suddenly rush together.

sanskrit: tato māṃ saṃparikṣipya sarvato vikṛtānanāḥ vadhe ca grahaṇe caiva kuryur yatnaṃ yathābalam
english: Then, surrounding me on all sides with their hideous faces, they would exert their full strength in killing or capturing me.

sanskrit: taṃ māṃ śākhāḥ praśākhāś ca skandhāṃś cottamaśākhinām dṛṣṭvā viparidhāvantaṃ bhaveyur bhayaśaṅkitāḥ
english: Seeing me leap about among the branches, sub-branches, and trunks of tall trees, they might become apprehensive with fear.

sanskrit: mama rūpaṃ ca saṃprekṣya vanaṃ vicarato mahat rākṣasyo bhayavitrastā bhaveyur vikṛtānanāḥ
english: And the demonesses with their hideous faces, beholding my great form as I roam through the forest, might be convulsed with fear.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuryuḥ samāhvānaṃ rākṣasyo rakṣasām api rākṣasendraniyuktānāṃ rākṣasendraniveśane
english: Then the demonesses would summon the rākṣasas as well — those posted by the lord of the rākṣasas within the abode of the lord of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: te śūlaśaranistriṃśa vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ āpateyur vimarde 'smin vegenodvignakāriṇaḥ
english: Those bearing in their hands spears, arrows, swords, and weapons of every kind would rush upon me in this combat, swift and causing alarm.

sanskrit: saṃkruddhas tais tu parito vidhaman rakṣasāṃ balam śaknuyaṃ na tu saṃprāptuṃ paraṃ pāraṃ mahodadheḥ
english: Though enraged and capable of scattering the forces of the rākṣasas on every side, I could not then reach the far shore of the great ocean.

sanskrit: māṃ vā gṛhṇīyur āplutya bahavaḥ śīghrakāriṇaḥ syād iyaṃ cāgṛhītārthā mama ca grahaṇaṃ bhavet
english: Or many swift-acting ones might leap upon me and seize me; the purpose would remain unaccomplished, and I would be captured.

sanskrit: hiṃsābhirucayo hiṃsyur imāṃ vā janakātmajām vipannaṃ syāt tataḥ kāryaṃ rāmasugrīvayor idam
english: Or those who delight in harm might harm Janaka's daughter — then this task of Rāma and Sugrīva would be ruined.

sanskrit: uddeśe naṣṭamārge 'smin rākṣasaiḥ parivārite sāgareṇa parikṣipte gupte vasati jānakī
english: Jānakī resides in this place where the path is lost, surrounded by rākṣasas, enclosed by the ocean, and closely guarded.

sanskrit: viśaste vā gṛhīte vā rakṣobhir mayi saṃyuge nānyaṃ paśyāmi rāmasya sahāyaṃ kāryasādhane
english: Whether I am slain or captured by the rākṣasas in battle, I see no other helper capable of accomplishing Rāma's task.

sanskrit: vimṛśaṃś ca na paśyāmi yo hate mayi vānaraḥ śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ laṅghayeta mahodadhim
english: Reflecting carefully, I see no other monkey who, if I were killed, could leap across the great ocean extending a hundred yojanas.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ hantuṃ samartho 'smi sahasrāṇy api rakṣasām na tu śakṣyāmi saṃprāptuṃ paraṃ pāraṃ mahodadheḥ
english: I am certainly capable of slaying even thousands of rākṣasas, but I would not then be able to reach the far shore of the great ocean.

sanskrit: asatyāni ca yuddhāni saṃśayo me na rocate kaś ca niḥsaṃśayaṃ kāryaṃ kuryāt prājñaḥ sasaṃśayam
english: And battles whose outcome is uncertain do not please me; what wise man would place certain success in jeopardy through a doubtful course of action?

sanskrit: eṣa doṣo mahān hi syān mama sītābhibhāṣaṇe prāṇatyāgaś ca vaidehyā bhaved anabhibhāṣaṇe
english: This is indeed a great danger in my speaking to Sītā; yet the abandonment of life by Vaidehī would be the danger in my not speaking.

sanskrit: bhūtāś cārthā vinaśyanti deśakālavirodhitāḥ viklavaṃ dūtam āsādya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā
english: Even accomplished purposes come to ruin when thwarted by wrong place and time, or when encountering a confused envoy — as darkness at sunrise.

sanskrit: arthānarthāntare buddhir niścitāpi na śobhate ghātayanti hi kāryāṇi dūtāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ
english: Even a resolute judgment fails to shine when it wavers between the right course and its ruin; for envoys who fancy themselves wise destroy their missions.

sanskrit: na vinaśyet kathaṃ kāryaṃ vaiklavyaṃ na kathaṃ bhavet laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya kathaṃ nu na vṛthā bhavet
english: How can this mission not be destroyed? How can confusion be avoided? And how may the crossing of the ocean not become in vain?

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu khalu vākyaṃ me śṛṇuyān nodvijeta ca iti saṃcintya hanumāṃś cakāra matimān matim
english: How indeed can she hear my words and yet not be alarmed? — pondering thus, the wise Hanūmān made up his mind.

sanskrit: rāmam akliṣṭakarmāṇaṃ svabandhum anukīrtayan nainām udvejayiṣyāmi tad bandhugatamānasām
english: Singing the praises of Rāma of tireless deeds, her own kinsman, I shall not disturb this lady whose heart is fixed upon that kinsman.

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ variṣṭhasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ śubhāni dharmayuktāni vacanāni samarpayan
english: Offering auspicious words full of righteousness about Rāma, the foremost of the Ikṣvākus, the self-knowing one —

sanskrit: śrāvayiṣyāmi sarvāṇi madhurāṃ prabruvan giram śraddhāsyati yathā hīyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ samādadhe
english: I shall cause her to hear all of them, speaking in a sweet voice; arranging everything in such a way that she may have faith.

sanskrit: iti sa bahuvidhaṃ mahānubhāvo jagatipateḥ pramadām avekṣamāṇaḥ madhuram avitathaṃ jagāda vākyaṃ drumaviṭapāntaram āsthito hanūmān
english: Thus having deliberated in many ways, the great-souled Hanūmān, gazing upon the wife of the lord of the world, perched within the foliage of the tree, spoke words that were sweet and true.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhāṃ cintāṃ cintayitva mahākapiḥ saṃśrave madhuraṃ vākyaṃ vaidehyā vyājahāra ha
english: Having thus considered his many thoughts, the great monkey spoke a sweet word within earshot of Vaidehī.

sanskrit: rājā daśaratho nāma rathakuñjaravājinām puṇyaśīlo mahākīrtir ṛjur āsīn mahāyaśāḥ cakravartikule jātaḥ puraṃdarasamo bale
english: There was a king named Daśaratha, foremost of those possessing chariots, elephants, and horses; of virtuous conduct and great fame, upright and of mighty glory, born in the lineage of universal sovereigns, equal in strength to Purandara.

sanskrit: ahiṃsāratir akṣudro ghṛṇī satyaparākramaḥ mukhyaś cekṣvākuvaṃśasya lakṣmīvāṃl lakṣmivardhanaḥ
english: Devoted to non-violence, not petty, compassionate, of true valor, the foremost of the Ikṣvāku lineage, possessed of prosperity and the increaser of prosperity.

sanskrit: pārthivavyañjanair yuktaḥ pṛthuśrīḥ pārthivarṣabhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ caturantayāṃ viśrutaḥ sukhadaḥ sukhī
english: Endowed with the marks of royalty, of broad renown, a bull among kings, renowned across the earth with its four quarters, a giver of happiness and himself happy.

sanskrit: tasya putraḥ priyo jyeṣṭhas tārādhipanibhānanaḥ rāmo nāma viśeṣajñaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: His beloved eldest son, whose face resembles the lord of the stars, named Rāma, skilled in discernment, the foremost of all wielders of the bow.

sanskrit: rakṣitā svasya vṛttasya svajanasyāpi rakṣitā rakṣitā jīvalokasya dharmasya ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: The scorcher of enemies, a guardian of his own conduct, a guardian of his own people, a guardian of the world of the living and of righteousness.

sanskrit: tasya satyābhisaṃdhasya vṛddhasya vacanāt pituḥ sabhāryaḥ saha ca bhrātrā vīraḥ pravrajito vanam
english: That hero, true to his pledges, at the word of his aged father, went forth with his wife and his brother into the forest.

sanskrit: tena tatra mahāraṇye mṛgayāṃ paridhāvatā janasthānavadhaṃ śrutvā hatau ca kharadūṣaṇau tatas tv amarṣāpahṛtā jānakī rāvaṇena tu
english: By him, ranging in that great forest in pursuit of game, was the slaughter at Janasthāna heard; and Khara and Dūṣaṇa were slain. Thereafter Jānakī was carried off by Rāvaṇa, overcome with fury.

sanskrit: yathārūpāṃ yathāvarṇāṃ yathālakṣmīṃ viniścitām aśrauṣaṃ rāghavasyāhaṃ seyam āsāditā mayā
english: As to her form, her complexion, her beauty as described and determined — I heard of her from Rāghava; and that very one has been reached by me here.

sanskrit: virarāmaivam uktvāsau vācaṃ vānarapuṃgavaḥ jānakī cāpi tac chrutvā vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatā
english: Having spoken thus, that bull among monkeys fell silent; and Jānakī, having heard those words, was filled with the utmost amazement.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā vakrakeśāntā sukeśī keśasaṃvṛtam unnamya vadanaṃ bhīruḥ śiṃśapāvṛkṣam aikṣata
english: Then she whose hair-ends were curled, the beautiful-haired one, trembling, raised her face — wrapped about by her hair — and looked up at the aśoka tree.

sanskrit: sā tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca tathāpy adhastān nirīkṣamāṇā tam acintya buddhim dadarśa piṅgādhipater amātyaṃ vātātmajaṃ sūryam ivodayastham
english: Looking sideways, upward, and also downward, she beheld the minister of the lord of the tawny ones — that son of the wind — of unimaginable intellect, like the sun at its rising.

sanskrit: tataḥ śākhāntare līnaṃ dṛṣṭvā calitamānasā sā dadarśa kapiṃ tatra praśritaṃ priyavādinam
english: Then, her mind stirred, seeing him concealed within the branches, she beheld there the monkey crouching humbly, ready to speak pleasant words.

sanskrit: sā tu dṛṣṭvā hariśreṣṭhaṃ vinītavad upasthitam maithilī cintayām āsa svapno 'yam iti bhāminī
english: But she, the passionate Maithilī, seeing the foremost of monkeys standing before her in a humble manner, thought to herself: 'This is a dream.'

sanskrit: sā taṃ samīkṣyaiva bhṛśaṃ visaṃjñā gatāsukalpeva babhūva sītā cireṇa saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya caiva vicintayām āsa viśālanetrā
english: Gazing intently at him, Sītā became profoundly overwhelmed, as if bereft of life; and after a time recovering her senses, the wide-eyed one began to reflect.

sanskrit: svapno mayāyaṃ vikṛto 'dya dṛṣṭaḥ śākhāmṛgaḥ śāstragaṇair niṣiddhaḥ svasty astu rāmāya salakṣmaṇāya tathā pitur me janakasya rājñaḥ
english: 'Today I have seen a strange dream — a tree-dwelling monkey, which the śāstras declare to be inauspicious. May there be well-being for Rāma, and likewise for Lakṣmaṇa, and for my father, King Janaka.'

sanskrit: svapno 'pi nāyaṃ na hi me 'sti nidrā śokena duḥkhena ca pīḍitāyāḥ sukhaṃ hi me nāsti yato 'smi hīnā tenendupūrṇapratimānanena
english: 'Yet this is not even a dream, for I have no sleep, tormented as I am by grief and sorrow. There is no happiness for me, since I am separated from him whose face is like the orb of the full moon.'

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi tasyādya mano bhavena saṃpīḍitā tad gatasarvabhāvā vicintayantī satataṃ tam eva tathaiva paśyāmi tathā śṛṇomi
english: 'I am now crushed by longing for him; my entire being is fixed upon him; ever meditating on him alone, I see him thus and I hear him thus.'

sanskrit: manorathaḥ syād iti cintayāmi tathāpi buddhyā ca vitarkayāmi kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya hi nāsti rūpaṃ suvyaktarūpaś ca vadaty ayaṃ mām
english: 'I think it may be a fancy of the mind; and yet I reason with my understanding: what is the cause? For there is no form of his here, yet this one with clearly distinct form speaks to me.'

sanskrit: namo 'stu vācaspataye savajriṇe svayambhuve caiva hutāśanāya anena coktaṃ yad idaṃ mamāgrato vanaukasā tac ca tathāstu nānyathā
english: 'Homage to Vācaspati, to the thunderbolt-wielding Indra, to the Self-born Brahmā, and to Fire — what this forest-dweller has spoken here before me, may that be true and not otherwise.'
